title: Terms
text: Three keys · Step 1 of 16 Terms ← Home Step 1 of 16 · Terms 2 · Before you begin → Time 10 min Difficulty Easy Steps 12 terms You will need: Nothing, just read The words you need before the work begins. Use these definitions as a reference throughout the guide. No secrets are needed to search. Find a term 12 terms shown. Seed phrase A human-readable backup used to derive wallet keys. Keep it secret. Recovery may also require a passphrase and, for multisig, the wallet configuration. Passphrase An additional secret used with a BIP39 seed phrase to derive a different wallet. The exact value matters: a typo can open a different, empty wallet. It is not the device PIN. Entropy Unpredictable input used to generate keys. Correct dice collection can provide entropy; it does not protect against malicious software that handles the result. BIP39 A specification for encoding entropy and a checksum as a mnemonic and deriving a seed from it, with an optional passphrase. It is more than a word list. Airgap Separation from networks. In this guide, secret-handling sessions use verified offline software. Turning networking off does not prove the computer is free of malware. Hash · file fingerprint A digest used to detect file changes. A match is useful only if the expected value comes from a trustworthy source; an attacker can replace both a file and its published hash. Digital signature A cryptographic check that a file was signed by a particular key and has not changed. Verify the signer’s key fingerprint independently; “Good signature” alone does not identify a trustworthy author. Extended public key · xpub Public information that can derive a branch of wallet addresses. It does not authorize spending on its own, but revealing it can expose wallet activity. Wallet descriptor A description of the scripts and public-key information used by a wallet. A watch-only descriptor is not a signing secret, but it is privacy-sensitive and important for multisig recovery. 2-of-3 multisig A wallet policy requiring signatures from two of three keys. Recovering with two seeds also needs the missing cosigner’s public information and the correct policy. PSBT Partially Signed Bitcoin Transaction: a format for carrying transaction details and signatures between wallet software and signers. It can be used with single-signature and multisig wallets. Watch-only wallet A wallet holding public information so it can display addresses and transactions. It cannot sign by itself. Verify its receive addresses against independently trusted wallet details. Independent verification: two matching tools are not enough if both rely on the same compromised input. Check the source of the data as well as the result. Specifications: BIP39 · PSBT (BIP174) . ← Home Step 1 of 16 2 · Before you begin →

title: Before you begin
text: Three keys · Step 2 of 16 Before you begin ← 1 · Terms Step 2 of 16 · Before you begin 3 · Pick your path → Time 5 min Difficulty Easy Steps 1 worksheet You will need: Pen and paper What are you protecting your Bitcoin from? Two quick questions help you identify your risks. No secret keys or personal information are collected. 1 Choose your concerns ✓ Theft Someone gets access to a backup. ✓ Fire or flood A backup location is destroyed. ✓ Mistakes I lose or record something incorrectly. ✓ Scams Someone tricks me into sharing a secret. ✓ Inheritance My family needs to recover my Bitcoin. 2 Where is your Bitcoin today? On an exchange Someone else controls the keys. Phone or software wallet My keys are on an internet-connected device. Hardware wallet I already use a dedicated signing device. I haven't started I want to begin correctly. Your security priorities Select the risks you want to plan for, then choose where your Bitcoin is today. These choices help you think through risks; they do not automatically determine a safe wallet configuration. Choose your path → Explore wallet risks and tradeoffs One key and a passphrase Simpler to operate, but forgetting or losing the passphrase can permanently prevent recovery. A compromised device or poorly stored backup can still put funds at risk. Keep the passphrase on paper apart from the plate. If someone finds both the seed backup and its passphrase, they may be able to access your funds. Keep them separately and test restoration. One device, one maker. A flawed or tampered device can still fail you. Words and passphrase go into the device itself during recovery, nowhere else. No hardware company will ever ask for your seed phrase. Check the receiving address on the device screen, not only on the computer screen, before you accept coins. The watch-only wallet cannot sign. Spending requires the signing key for the passphrase-protected wallet; recovery requires the seed and the exact passphrase. A replacement compatible device can be used. Three keys (2-of-3 multisig) Separates signing keys across devices or locations, but makes setup and recovery more complicated. Securely preserve the wallet configuration/descriptor and test the recovery procedure. Most steps to get right. A missed step in any key can lock the wallet later. If fewer than two signing keys remain available, you cannot spend, even with the wallet map. Losing the map can also prevent recovery when the missing public-key information cannot be reconstructed. Keep three plates in three places, and keep the encrypted map apart from any single plate. Two signing keys meet the 2-of-3 threshold, but recovery also requires the correct wallet configuration. Keep verified copies of the descriptor and recovery instructions in separate safe locations, and rehearse reconstruction and spending before funding the wallet. No passphrase on the 2-of-3. The protection comes from three keys in three places, not from a passphrase. Practice spend first, and rehearse on testnet if you have not done this before. Savings do not move until the practice spend works. Shut down fully between keys. A key left in memory is a key at risk. Note: One stolen seed being insufficient applies to an appropriately configured 2-of-3 multisig, not all wallets. Multisig does not automatically solve scams, user error, coercion, or inheritance. Test recovery before trusting a wallet with meaningful funds. Never type seed phrases or passphrases into a website, form, or demo. ← 1 · Terms Step 2 of 16 3 · Pick your path →

title: Checklist
text: Three keys · Step 4 of 16 Checklist ← 3 · Pick your path Step 4 of 16 · Checklist 5 · Two boots → Prepare the materials and the recovery plan before creating keys. Private workspace Fair dice with readable faces, a fixed reading order, a numbered recording sheet, and a pen. A workspace without cameras, microphones, or observers recording secrets. Time to stop and investigate any mismatch without rushing. Verified offline setup Prepare the Tails USB and a separate transfer USB. Read Two boots and Check the files before using downloads. Transfer media must never carry signing secrets back online. The kit contains version-pinned instructions. Confirm that each release, signature and hash belong together; do not substitute a newer binary while keeping an old manifest. Compatibility and version reconciliation remain under review. Backup materials Plan durable backups for three independently created signing seeds, one seed per clearly identified backup. Choose locations so one event does not expose or destroy a signing quorum. Choose a backup format you can read and test. Product capacity varies; this guide does not require a particular brand or forbid additional secured copies. Recovery records Preserve a verified public descriptor or compatible wallet-configuration backup containing all three cosigners’ public information, key origins, derivation paths and the 2-of-3 policy. Two seeds alone do not supply the missing cosigner’s public information. Prepare a private location record and instructions a trusted helper can understand. Rehearse with a disposable test wallet before relying on the process for savings. Before proceeding: review how you will recover at least two signing keys and the complete 2-of-3 wallet configuration. Having the equipment is not proof that the wallet is recoverable. ← 3 · Pick your path Step 4 of 16 5 · Two boots →

title: Two boots
text: Three keys · Step 5 of 16 Two boots ← 4 · Checklist Step 5 of 16 · Two boots 6 · Check the files → Time 45 min Difficulty Careful Steps 4 sections You will need: Everyday computer · Tails USB Separate online preparation from offline secret handling. This page explains the session boundaries. Read Check the files and complete verification before installing or running downloaded software. Page order is not permission to skip that check. Limits: Tails and Offline Mode cannot make compromised hardware or firmware trustworthy. Reusing one computer for several keys creates shared risks that a reboot does not remove. Online preparation Download and verify first Follow the official Tails installation instructions for your computer and release. Authenticate the image before writing it. Keep a separate data USB for the specific verified files you need. Do not put seed phrases, raw entropy, private keys, or passphrases on the data USB or in the everyday operating system. Do not create or unlock Persistent Storage for this guide’s temporary secret-handling sessions. Offline session Set the boundary before secrets At the Tails Welcome Screen, enable Offline Mode before starting the desktop. Older instructions may call this networking disabled. Disconnect network cables and do not enable networking during the session. Use only the verified local tools required for the task. A webpage’s “offline” badge is a reminder, not proof of network isolation or a safe computer. One key or three? The one-key path creates one seed. The three-key path uses a separate session for each seed. Do not load multiple signing seeds in one session. Separate sessions reduce accidental mixing; they do not establish independent hardware trust. Transfer boundary Export only what the next step needs When the guide calls for a transfer, export only reviewed public wallet information or the required transaction file. Public descriptors and xpubs expose wallet activity and still need privacy protection. Never copy seeds, raw entropy, private-key exports, or secret-bearing wallet files back to the online computer. Do not assume a file is public because its name says “backup.” Inspect the export type and follow the wallet’s documentation. End the session Power off fully Finish the offline task and shut down Tails completely before another key session. Do not substitute suspend or hibernate. Keep your physical backup private, away from cameras and microphones. Shutdown ends the session; it does not undo a disclosure, erase a file you saved elsewhere, or remove malicious firmware. If isolation or software integrity is in doubt, stop and investigate before using that key. Stop if: verification is incomplete, networking was enabled while a secret was present, a secret was saved to transfer media, or you cannot identify what an export contains. Do not use a real funded wallet for a rehearsal. Official references: Welcome Screen and Offline Mode · Untrusted computer risks . Next, Check the files. Return to these session rules when the later steps require offline work. ← 4 · Checklist Step 5 of 16 6 · Check the files →

title: Check the files
text: Three keys · Step 6 of 16 Check the files ← 5 · Two boots Step 6 of 16 · Check the files 7 · Make three keys → Time 30 min Difficulty Careful Steps 7 sections You will need: The downloaded files · Two verification tools Verify the file, its source, and the signing key before running it. Staging guide: a familiar domain or HTTPS connection does not certify software safety. This site’s tools and instructions remain under review. Never enter signing secrets into the live website. 1 · Source Start with the project Use the developer’s official download and verification instructions for the exact release and operating system. Avoid links from advertisements, unsolicited messages, or search-result lookalikes. For this kit, the downloads page and manifest identify distributed files. They do not independently audit their code. What HTTPS tells you HTTPS protects the connection to the named domain. It does not prove that the domain, its publisher, or the downloaded program is trustworthy. 2 · Integrity Compare the complete hash Calculate the downloaded file’s SHA-256 digest and compare every character with the authenticated expected value for that exact release. The file checker can compare a kit file with its listed digest. A match means the bytes agree with the reference. If an attacker replaces both the file and the reference, that comparison will still pass. Command-line alternatives On macOS, use shasum -a 256 followed by the file path. In Windows PowerShell, use Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 with the file path. Follow the project’s instructions for your platform. 3 · Authenticity Verify the signer, then the signature Where the publisher provides signatures, authenticate the signing key’s full fingerprint using the publisher’s documented verification process and an independently trusted source. Then verify the signature for the exact downloaded file or signed checksum manifest. “Good signature” alone is insufficient. It means the signature verifies under a key; you must establish whose key it is. A new key or unexplained fingerprint change needs investigation. About trust warnings A message that a key is not certified can reflect your local trust settings. Do not dismiss it without independently checking the key identity. Stop for a bad signature, unexpected key, or unresolved warning. 4 · Ready to proceed? Keep a verification record Record the release, file name, hash, verification method, and signing-key fingerprint when applicable. Run any kit verification script only after reviewing and authenticating that script too. Never run a failed or unexplained download. Recheck the source and release before trying again. A successful checksum or signature does not establish that software is bug-free or appropriate for custody. Stop if: the source is uncertain, a hash differs, a signature fails, the key identity is unverified, or the release cannot be matched to its verification instructions. Do not proceed to secret-handling work. Use the current official instructions: Tails installation · Sparrow downloads and verification . Next, follow your path’s key-generation page. Verify every required file before opening an offline secret-handling session. ← 5 · Two boots Step 6 of 16 7 · Make three keys →

title: Make three keys
text: Three keys · Step 7 of 16 Make the three keys ← 6 · Check the files Step 7 of 16 · Make three keys 8 · Build the 2-of-3 → Time 30-45 min Difficulty Moderate Steps 6 sections You will need: 5 dice · Paper and pen · The worksheet You will roll dice to create three separate Bitcoin seed phrases. Each one becomes 24 words. The computer never sees the network while you work. Safety first: Never enter seed words on an online computer. Boot Tails with networking Disabled before you start. Shut down fully between each key. What you will do Boot Tails offline. Copy the dice converter page. Roll dice. Enter the faces. The page counts to 256 bits. Write down the 24 words. Prove them with a second tool. Repeat for Seed 2 and Seed 3, with a full shutdown between each. Step 1 / 6 Boot Tails. Copy the converter. Boot Tails with networking set to Disabled. Copy the checked dice converter page from the data USB to the Desktop. Check: Open only the verified local copy after enabling Tails Offline Mode. An offline indicator alone does not prove network isolation. If it reports online, stop. Step 2 / 6 Roll the dice. Enter the faces. Roll five dice at once. Enter each face as you roll it. Using fair, independently rolled dice and a fixed reading order, faces 1 to 4 count as bits (1=00, 2=01, 3=10, 4=11). Faces 5 and 6 are skipped, roll those dice again. The page counts the pairs and stops you at 128. SHAKE 1 SHAKE 2 SHAKE 3 11 RE-ROLL 01 00 10 01 01 RE-ROLL 11 11 00 10 00 10 RE-ROLL 00 01 RE-ROLL 10 256-BIT STRING 11 00 10 01 01 01 11 00 10 11 00 10 00 01 10 …keep rolling… 256 / 256 BITS 10 / 256 20 / 256 30 / 256 256 / 256 24 WORDS Roll as many times as needed to get 256 bits of entropy: about 39 shakes. Check: The page shows 128 pairs and 256 bits. Count accepted pairs, not an estimated number of shakes. Step 3 / 6 Write the 24 words. At 256 bits the page prints 24 words. In a 24-word BIP39 phrase, the last word contains three entropy bits and eight checksum bits. It is not an arbitrary check word: never invent or alter it. Write all 24 on the grid. Compare them privately in order, away from cameras and microphones. Check: All 24 words and their positions are recorded accurately; a valid checksum does not prove safe randomness. Step 4 / 6 Prove it with a second tool. Use a separately verified offline implementation with the exact same 256-bit entropy and BIP39 settings. Raw dice inputs are not interchangeable between tools: some hash the roll string while this guide maps accepted faces to bit pairs. Confirm the input method before comparing all 24 words. If you cannot establish that the inputs and method match, stop; do not guess or choose a preferred output. Check: Both tools show the same 24 words. Step 5 / 6 Shut down. Start the next key. Shut Tails down fully. Wait until the screen is dark. Then boot again for Seed 2. New rolls, new words. Repeat for Seed 3. Never continue a list from the previous boot. Check: Each seed has its own 24 words on its own grid. Three grids total. Step 6 / 6 Confirm the checks agree. The checksum detects many transcription errors, but not all of them. It does not authenticate the source of the words. At least two checks must agree: the two tools showing the same words, and the wallet (Sparrow or Electrum, offline) opening the list without error. If anything disagrees, stop. Stop if: The page says online. The two tools show different words. The wallet rejects the list. Any of these means stop and start that key over. Next, Build the 2-of-3. ← 6 · Check the files Step 7 of 16 8 · Build the 2-of-3 →

title: Build the 2-of-3
text: Three keys · Step 8 of 16 Build the 2-of-3 ← 7 · Make three keys Step 8 of 16 · Build the 2-of-3 9 · Practice spend → Time 45-60 min Difficulty Careful Steps 7 steps You will need: The three paper keys · Verified Sparrow The final watch-only wallet is built from three public keys. Earlier steps use one seed per offline boot to obtain each public key. What comes out is the wallet map, which can watch the money and never spend it. Safety first: Never enter seed words on an online computer. You will boot Tails four times: once per seed to copy its public key, then once more with no seed to build the vault. Files used: Sparrow 2.5.5. Tails 7.16 or later 7.x (verified). Electrum 4.8.3 for the cross-check. What you will do Boot Tails offline. Launch Sparrow from the terminal. Extract each seed's public key, one per boot. Build the 2-of-3 vault with no seed. Export the map. Independently verify the cosigners and wallet policy, then compare several receiving addresses. Step 1 / 7 Boot Tails. Networking stays off. The entire sheet happens with networking Disabled. Check it on every boot. Step 2 / 7 Open the terminal. Launch Sparrow. Run these commands one at a time. Wait for each command to finish before entering the next. The shell prompt is not part of a command. cd ~/Desktop tar -xvf sparrowwallet-2.5.5-x86_64.tar.gz cd Sparrow ./bin/Sparrow Sparrow may take 15 to 30 seconds to open. The terminal may remain occupied while Sparrow runs. If a command reports an error or the expected window does not open, stop and investigate; text color alone is not an error check. Step 3 / 7 New wallet: 2 of 3, native Segwit. File → New Wallet. Pick Multi Signature, Native Segwit, 2 of 3. The path must read m/48'/0'/0'/2' . Anything else: stop. Check: The path reads exactly m/48'/0'/0'/2' . Step 4 / 7 Keystore 1: Seed 1 in, public key out. Keystore 1 → New or Imported Software Wallet → type Seed 1's 24 words. Export the xpub. Save it to the data USB as s1-xpub.txt . Close Sparrow. Shut down. Wait for a dark screen. Step 5 / 7 Twice more. One seed per boot. Boot again for Seed 2 → s2-xpub.txt . Shut down. Boot again for Seed 3 → s3-xpub.txt . Shut down. Check: Three xpub files on the USB. One seed per boot, never two. Step 6 / 7 Fresh boot. No seed. Build the vault. Boot Tails again. Do not type any seed. New wallet → Multi Signature → Native Segwit → 2 of 3 → import the three xpub files. Confirm the path. Export the output descriptor to the data USB. That file is the wallet map. Step 7 / 7 · Before funding Verify the wallet independently Matching addresses alone cannot prove a coordinator is honest if both devices use the same unverified descriptor. 01 · Record addresses Record several complete receiving addresses from Sparrow offline. Write the full strings, not just QR codes. 02 · Verify each cosigner On a separate trusted offline device, compare each cosigner’s master fingerprint, derivation path, and extended public key with records obtained directly from that signer—not solely from the coordinator. 03 · Check the wallet policy Confirm the 2-of-3 threshold, native SegWit script type, and full descriptor including key order and checksum where supported. 04 · Rebuild and compare Reconstruct a watch-only wallet from independently verified details. Compare several receiving addresses character for character. Never enter seeds on a networked device. Stop before funding if anything differs. If a key, fingerprint, path, policy, or address differs, investigate offline. Two devices using the same substituted descriptor may show matching attacker-controlled addresses. Next, Practice spend. ← 7 · Make three keys Step 8 of 16 9 · Practice spend →

title: Practice spend
text: Three keys · Step 9 of 16 Practice spend ← 8 · Build the 2-of-3 Step 9 of 16 · Practice spend 10 · Metal and the map → Time 45 min Difficulty Careful Steps 5 sections You will need: Two seeds · Tails USB · A small test amount THE AIRGAP SHUTDOWN · NEW SESSION ONLINE OFFLINE CREATE TRANSACTION BROADCAST TRANSACTION SEED 1 SEED 2 1 OF 2 2 OF 2 1 Create. Watch-only builds the transaction. The file is an empty outline. 2 Seed 1 signs. The file fills halfway. 1 of 2. 3 Shutdown. The file stops at the red line: full shutdown, new session, then crosses deliberately. 4 Seed 2 signs. The file fills whole. 2 of 2. 5 Broadcast. Up and right, across the airgap. The twice-signed file goes out. The practice spend uses a small amount, enough to pay a fee and no more. Write the destination, amount, and fee on paper before anything is exported. Safety first: Never enter seed words on an online computer. Read your paper notes again before each signature. Files used: Sparrow 2.5.5. Tails 7.16 or later 7.x (verified). What you will do Build the spend on the online watch-only wallet. Sign with Seed 1 on Tails. Shut down. Sign with Seed 2 on a fresh boot. Shut down. Broadcast from the online computer. Step 1 / 4 Build the spend (online, watch-only). Open watch-only Sparrow. Send tab: destination, amount, fee. Finalize for signing. Export tx-unsigned.psbt to the data USB. Step 2 / 4 Seed 1 signs (Tails, networking off). Boot Tails, networking disabled. Restore Seed 1 only. Open tx-unsigned.psbt , confirm the fields against the paper, sign. Export tx-partial-s1.psbt . Full shutdown. Step 3 / 4 Seed 2 signs (fresh boot). Fresh Tails boot. Restore Seed 2 only. Open tx-partial-s1.psbt . Confirm the first signature and that the spend is unchanged. Sign. Export tx-signed.psbt . Full shutdown. Check: Two signatures. The destination and amount match your paper. Step 4 / 4 Broadcast (online computer). On the online computer, open the signed transaction and broadcast it. Watch for confirmation. Stop if: The fields don't match your paper. A signature is missing. Networking was on during signing. ← 8 · Build the 2-of-3 Step 9 of 16 10 · Metal and the map →

title: Metal and the map
text: Three keys · Step 10 of 16 Metal and the map ← 9 · Practice spend Step 10 of 16 · Metal and the map 11 · Rehearse on testnet → Make a durable backup without losing the ability to recover. Record accurately Back up each of the three seeds separately using the chosen medium’s instructions. Preserve word order and any required encoding information. Work privately and compare every entry against the original. Keep the original protected while checking the replacement. A damaged or ambiguous mark needs correction before you rely on it. Check recovery safely Use the wallet’s documented backup-check or recovery procedure on trusted equipment. Do not wipe your only working signer to test an unproven backup. Never type seeds into this website or an online form. For a rehearsal, use a disposable test wallet. For an existing funded wallet, plan the verification carefully before changing devices or backups. Keep the complete recovery information Preserve a verified public descriptor or compatible wallet-configuration backup containing all three cosigners’ public information, key origins, derivation paths and the 2-of-3 policy. Two seeds alone do not supply the missing cosigner’s public information. A public-only descriptor cannot sign by itself, but it reveals wallet information. Confirm that the export contains no private keys before treating it as public data. Protect its availability and privacy. Plan copies and locations Balance loss, theft, access, and disaster risks. More copies can improve availability and also expose secrets in more places. Document which locations contain which material; do not combine enough signing secrets in one place to defeat your separation plan. Do not destroy an original merely because a new backup looks correct. Retire it only after a successful recovery check and a deliberate review of the remaining copies. Revisit the plan when locations or helpers change. Stop if: a backup is unreadable, the recovered wallet differs, or any required passphrase or configuration is missing. Do not overwrite or discard the remaining working material. ← 9 · Practice spend Step 10 of 16 11 · Rehearse on testnet →

title: Rehearse on testnet
text: Three keys · Step 11 of 16 Rehearse on testnet ← 10 · Metal and the map Step 11 of 16 · Rehearse on testnet 12 · Protect the wallet map → Time 30 min Difficulty Moderate Steps 2 sections You will need: Sparrow · Free testnet coins Before any plate exists, do the entire flow with play money: build the 2-of-3, receive, sign with two keys, shut down between sessions, broadcast. The clicks are identical to mainnet. Safety first: Testnet coins are worthless. They cannot be sold or spent as real bitcoin. That is the point. Do not "test" with real bitcoin. Files used: Sparrow 2.5.5. What you will do Get testnet coins from a faucet. Build a throwaway 2-of-3. Receive the coins. Sign with two keys, with a shutdown between. Broadcast. Then burn the test seeds. Step 1 / 2 Run the rehearsal. Get testnet coins. Make a testnet address in Sparrow, paste it into a faucet, wait for confirmation. Build the 2-of-3. Generate three throwaway test seeds. Import them, build the 2-of-3, verify the first address on a second screen. Receive and sign. Send the tBTC to your test wallet. Build a small spend, sign with key 1, shut down, boot fresh, sign with key 2, broadcast. Check: The transaction confirms on a testnet explorer. You completed the whole loop. Step 2 / 2 Burn the test seeds. Never reuse test seeds on mainnet. When the rehearsal is done, the test seeds are burned. They do not get stamped, written down, or kept. Stop if: You're tempted to use real bitcoin for the rehearsal. You're tempted to keep a test seed. Graduate when: You built, received, two-key-signed across a shutdown, and broadcast, without the sheet open. The plates come after you're bored of succeeding on testnet. ← 10 · Metal and the map Step 11 of 16 12 · Protect the wallet map →

title: Protect the wallet map
text: Three keys · Step 12 of 16 Hide the wallet map ← 11 · Rehearse on testnet Step 12 of 16 · Protect the wallet map 13 · If I am gone → Time 30 min Difficulty Careful Steps 5 steps You will need: descriptor-tool.html (verified) · A dice passphrase Geography 3 seeds, secured separately in 3 different locations HOUSE 1 Plate A Seed 1 only Home safe / fire box Wallet map lives here too (the map is not a third seed) HOUSE 2 Plate B Seed 2 only Different building, different risk A copy of the map may sit here HOUSE 3 Plate C Seed 3 only Another town or trusted party Do not park Seed 1 or 2 here Geography: three plates in three places. No single point of failure. At a glance. Time: 30 minutes. Difficulty: Careful. Steps: 5. Boot Tails. Copy the tool and the map. Open the tool. Encrypt the map. Copy the locked file. Delete the plain one. Write the passphrase on paper. Twice. Prove it opens. Check the first address. The map can watch the money, but it cannot spend. Anyone who can read it can see the balance, so it never sits around as plain text. Files used: Tails 7.16 or later 7.x (verified). Get the descriptor tool Download the descriptor tool page. Save it. Check its fingerprint on the verify page before you copy it to your data USB. Open descriptor tool (HTML) The Python script is the backup check. It lives in the kit. Make a passphrase with dice Roll five dice. Read the faces left to right. Look the five-digit number up in the EFF word list. Write the word down. Do this six times. Six words give about 77 bits. Use the word list or the Diceware mapper from a saved copy, on Tails with networking disabled. Never in an everyday browser. Watch how it works: Open the demo full screen Write the six words on paper, in two separate places. Never stamp a passphrase on a plate. Never keep it with the plate, the map, or the USBs. Seed words and passphrase words use different dice methods. Seeds keep faces 1 to 4 and reroll 5 and 6. Passphrases keep all six faces, no rerolls. A passphrase word is never a seed word. Step 1 · Boot Tails. Copy the tool and the map. Open the demo full screen TAILS network off DESKTOP descriptor-tool.html map.txt NEVER OPEN THE MAP ON A PHONE Boot Tails, networking Disabled. Copy the tool page and map.txt to the Desktop. Step 2 · Open the tool. Encrypt the map. Open the demo full screen Descriptor tool Offline Encrypt a map Decrypt a map Drop map.txt here, or paste the text Passphrase: •••••••••• (twice) Download map.txt.asc ✓ Open the tool page. It checks the computer is offline before it starts. Choose Encrypt a map. Drop map.txt on the page or paste the text. Enter your passphrase twice. Review, then Encrypt. Download map.txt.asc. Step 3 · Copy the locked file. Delete the plain one. map.txt.asc 🔒 locked USB 1 USB 2 map.txt 🗑 EMPTY THE TRASH Copy map.txt.asc to two USB drives. Delete map.txt from the Desktop and the USB. Empty the trash. Step 4 · Write the passphrase on paper. Twice. PASSPHRASE place #1 PASSPHRASE place #2 AWAY FROM THE PLATES · AWAY FROM THE USBs Two copies, two separate places. This paper unlocks every encrypted copy of the map. Treat it like a plate. Step 5 · Prove it opens. Check the first address. Decrypt a map (later offline boot) Passphrase: •••••••••• first address: bc1q…7x2k ✓ MATCHES On a later offline boot, open the tool again. Choose Decrypt a map. Paste the armored text. Enter the passphrase once. The restored map must match, and the first address must match what you wrote down. If the passphrase is lost, the coins aren't gone, as long as all three plates still exist. Three seeds rebuild the map. Two cannot. Stop if The tool says the computer is online: stop. Do not type the passphrase. You want the xpubs on paper "just in case": that's a leak. Stop. You want to invent your own cipher: stop. Use the tool. Next, If I am gone. ← 11 · Rehearse on testnet Step 12 of 16 13 · If I am gone →

title: If I am gone
text: Three keys · Step 13 of 16 If I am gone ← 12 · Protect the wallet map Step 13 of 16 · If I am gone 14 · If you get stuck → Help a trusted person understand what to find—and when to stop. Leave a clear private plan Describe the wallet type, the location of the full instructions, the required recovery items, and a trusted contact who can explain the process. Keep signing secrets out of this website, email, and the general instruction sheet. Separate ownership and access arrangements from the technical recovery instructions. Make sure the intended person can find the plan when needed. Identify the required items This path requires at least two signing keys and the complete 2-of-3 wallet configuration. Preserve a verified public descriptor or compatible wallet-configuration backup containing all three cosigners’ public information, key origins, derivation paths and the 2-of-3 policy. Two seeds alone do not supply the missing cosigner’s public information. Keep each signing seed on a separate compatible signer during the planned hardware-wallet recovery. Do not assume an arbitrary replacement device supports the recorded policy. Check compatibility before importing secrets. Confirm the recovered wallet Follow the recorded, rehearsed procedure and verify the policy and wallet details against independent trusted records. An address match alone does not establish that a coordinator is trustworthy. If the wallet is empty or differs from the records, stop. Check the passphrase, account, network, derivation information and synchronization before concluding funds are lost. Do not overwrite backups or create replacement keys as a guess. Practice before an emergency Walk through locating the records and explaining the steps with the intended helper. Use a disposable test wallet for hands-on training, without exposing the owner’s signing secrets. When a legitimate recovery is needed, independently verify the destination and transaction details on trusted signing equipment. A small successful transfer is useful evidence, but it is not a complete audit of the recovery setup. Protect the secrets: no legitimate support agent needs a seed phrase or private key. If the instructions, equipment compatibility, or wallet identity are uncertain, stop before entering secrets or signing. ← 12 · Protect the wallet map Step 13 of 16 14 · If you get stuck →

title: If you get stuck
text: Three keys · Step 14 of 16 If you get stuck ← 13 · If I am gone Step 14 of 16 · If you get stuck 15 · Tough questions → Time 10 min Difficulty Easy Steps 7 questions You will need: Nothing, find your question Find the question that matches your problem. When in doubt, stop is always a valid step. What am I actually making? Three keys, made at home with dice, on a computer with no internet. Any two can spend; one cannot. The keys are stamped into titanium and kept in three places. A hardware wallet is optional, and it never creates the keys. I already own a hardware wallet. Do I start there? No. It stays in the drawer until the plates exist and a small payment has moved. If a key later goes on a device, the second key goes on a different maker’s device. All three never go on hardware. The plates are the backup. The download is newer than the version on the sheet. Stop. Sparrow and Electrum must match the version on the sheet exactly. A newer Sparrow or Electrum file is a stop. Delete it. Tails is different. Download the latest Tails 7.x release from tails.net, and verify its signature and checksum. If either check fails, or if any boot step differs from the guide, stop. Delete the file. A Tails 8 release is not covered. It needs a guide update first. The two word lists don’t match. Stop. Don’t pick the nicer list. Don’t “fix” word 24. Roll again or find the copying mistake. A fixed word is a destroyed key. Can I keep the words in a password manager? No. A photo, note, password manager, or email is one hacked account from the whole seed. Words go on metal. The map is encrypted; its passphrase is on paper, away from the plates. What if the map, or its passphrase, is lost? Three plates rebuild the map exactly, so the coins aren’t gone. But two plates cannot . The third key can’t be derived from the other two. Back up the passphrase paper in two places, away from the plates. (Full rule on the map sheet.) What does my family do? Hand them the “If I am gone” sheet. Two plates and the map. A Jade and a BitBox from the makers’ own shops, one plate per device. No Tails. No typing words into a phone. ← 13 · If I am gone Step 14 of 16 15 · Tough questions →

title: Tough questions
text: Three keys · Step 15 of 16 Tough questions ← 14 · If you get stuck Step 15 of 16 · Tough questions 16 · Recovery card → Time 15 min Difficulty Easy Steps 6 questions You will need: Nothing, read and discuss You typed the seed on a laptop. Isn’t that exposed? Typed on Tails, networking off, one seed per boot, then a full shutdown. Tails forgets the session. A hardware keylogger is still possible. But one captured seed still can’t spend : the fund needs two. Never type two seeds on one boot. Why not start with a hardware wallet? A signer can join later; it is not how these keys are made. The randomness is dice you can watch . No chip to trust, no firmware to audit. Is dice randomness weaker than a hardware RNG? No. 256 bits is 256 bits , whatever made them. If the map passphrase is lost, are the coins gone? Not with all three plates. They rebuild the map exactly. But two plates plus a lost passphrase means the addresses are unrecoverable . Back up the passphrase paper in two places, away from the plates and USBs. What if someone finds one plate? They can’t spend. One key alone opens nothing. But never keep two plates in one place : that’s the whole lock in one drawer. Shouldn’t I add a passphrase to the multisig? No. The security is the distribution , not one more secret. A passphrase on the 2-of-3 is a single point of failure in disguise. Lose it and two plates aren’t enough. The home plate’s small decoy wallet is the separate, optional place for a passphrase. ← 14 · If you get stuck Step 15 of 16 16 · Recovery card →

title: Recovery card
text: Three keys · Step 16 of 16 Recovery card ← 15 · Tough questions Step 16 of 16 · Recovery card Review this path → A private pointer to your recovery plan—not a wallet backup. What this card is for A short location record helps an authorized person find the complete instructions and required materials. It cannot replace at least two signing keys and the complete 2-of-3 wallet configuration. Location information can help a thief too. Protect the card even though it contains no signing secrets. Write these pointers offline Wallet type: 2-of-3 multisig. Where to find the complete recovery instructions. Separate seed-backup locations and wallet-configuration location. Trusted contact and date last reviewed. Location of any separate decryption instructions, if required. Write privately on paper. This page intentionally provides no form for entering real locations or secrets. Never include these No seed words, raw entropy, private keys, wallet passphrases, or decryption passwords on the card. Keep it separate from the materials it points to. A descriptor can contain private keys; only a verified public-only export belongs in the non-signing configuration records. Keep it current Check that the intended person can follow the pointers. Update the record after moving a backup or changing the recovery plan, then account for obsolete copies. The downloadable legacy card/PDF has not yet been reconciled with these revised instructions. Do not treat that older packet as a verified version of this page. Recovery still requires verification: use the complete, rehearsed procedure. A list of locations, a device brand, or a derivation-path label is not sufficient by itself. ← 15 · Tough questions Step 16 of 16 Review this path →
